articles.title: chmod 755 Is Not 'Read, Write, Execute': 5 Permission Traps
articles.excerpt: Every tutorial hands you the same two commands: chmod 755 for directories, chmod 644 for files. Both work. Neither explains what you just agreed to. I built a small permissions calculator while cleani…
articles.body: Every tutorial hands you the same two commands: chmod 755 for directories, chmod 644 for files. Both work. Neither explains what you just agreed to. I built a small permissions calculator while cleaning up a deploy script, and these are the traps that bit me hardest — every number below I re-ran in a shell today. 1. rwx on a directory is not about the files On a regular file the three bits are obvious. On a directory they mean something else entirely: r lists names, w creates and deletes entries, x lets you traverse — stat a child, cd into it, open anything inside. I set a directory to 666 and got exactly that behaviour: listing it returned an empty result without an error, creating a file inside failed with EACCES, and cd into it failed too. Readable but useless.
articles.author: zhihu wu

articles.title: Same loop, same numbers, 13x slower. I only swapped two lines.
articles.excerpt: Two functions that add up every number in a 4096 by 4096 grid: function sumRows(grid) { let s = 0; for (let r = 0; r < N; r++) for (let c = 0; c < N; c++) s += grid[r][c]; return s; } function sumCols…
articles.body: Two functions that add up every number in a 4096 by 4096 grid: function sumRows ( grid ) { let s = 0 ; for ( let r = 0 ; r < N ; r ++ ) for ( let c = 0 ; c < N ; c ++ ) s += grid [ r ][ c ]; return s ; } function sumCols ( grid ) { let s = 0 ; for ( let c = 0 ; c < N ; c ++ ) for ( let r = 0 ; r < N ; r ++ ) s += grid [ r ][ c ]; return s ; } Same grid. Same 16.7 million additions. Same answer. The only difference is which loop is on the outside. On my laptop (Node 24, Apple M3), median of 5 runs: sumRows 11 ms sumCols 146 ms 13 times slower. Nothing in the code tells you that. The CPU never reads just one number Reading from RAM takes around 100 nanoseconds. In that time the CPU could do hundreds of additions. So it cheats.
articles.author: Thới Hải Đức

articles.title: A job offer on LinkedIn came with malware in a Git hook. It's the "Contagious Interview" playbook
articles.excerpt: A recruiter messaged me on LinkedIn about building the website for a blockchain basketball game. Then they sent a documentation pack as a .tar.gz file. The plan was simple: review the docs, sign the N…
articles.body: A recruiter messaged me on LinkedIn about building the website for a blockchain basketball game. Then they sent a documentation pack as a .tar.gz file. The plan was simple: review the docs, sign the NDA, then we'd schedule a call. The docs were real enough to read. The archive also held a Git hook that would have downloaded a script and run it on my Mac the first time I checked out a branch. One of its branches was called NDA . It follows the playbook of a campaign security researchers have been tracking for a while, called Contagious Interview : fake recruiters, web3 projects, and code that runs when a developer does something routine. With so many developers looking for work right now, I'm writing up exactly what it looked like, so it's easier to spot.
articles.author: Huzaifa Khan

articles.body: 「我的 GPU endpoint 有哪些還在計費？」這個問題很簡單，但要回答它，通常得點進三個畫面、讀出數字，再回到聊天視窗把它們打出來。把這件事交給 AI 代理聽起來很不錯，直到你開始追問：它到底點了什麼？osFoundry Operator 就是圍繞這個問題設計的：代理在對話旁邊的 App 即時窗格裡工作，它做的每個動作都會被記錄下來。 對話旁邊，就是 App 的即時窗格 osFoundry 是一款把聊天、代理、檔案和工具整合在同一個視窗裡的桌面 App。Operator 把畫面分成三欄。左邊是 Operator 的工作階段清單，中間是對話，右邊則是即時的 dashboard 窗格：一份真正的 osFoundry App，Operator 會在裡面開啟各個畫面。窗格上方會顯示目前所在的畫面（這裡是 Dashboard /models/endpoints），並提供 Home 與 Project 捷徑、Reload dashboard 和 Open in a new window。拖曳分隔線就能把窗格拉寬。 在這個例子裡，Sammy 問哪些 GPU endpoint 正在計費。Operator 在窗格中開啟 Endpoints，讀取上面的卡片，然後在聊天中回答：一個 endpoint 是 Active，每小時 $1.45，目前已花費 $7.54；一個還在 Creating，但已經開始計費；另一個是 Stopped。答案來自它剛剛開啟的畫面，而那個畫面還留在原處，隨時可以核對。它也主動提議停止那個運作中的 endpoint，並表示按下 Stop 之前會先詢問。 活動列：Operator 實際做了什麼 窗格下方有一條細長的活動列，顯示 Operator 目前是閒置還是工作中，以及上次動作的時間。展開之後，Log 會列出 Operator 在這個窗格中做過的所有動作，最新的在最上…

articles.body: AI 에이전트와의 채팅은 한 번으로 끝나는 일에는 충분합니다. 하지만 계속 이어지는 일은 다릅니다. 매주 진행 보고서, 출시 때마다 나가는 보도자료, 매일 하는 경쟁사 체크. 각각 담당이 있어야 하고, 정해진 시간에 돌아가야 하고, 기자 42명에게 메일 보내기처럼 되돌릴 수 없는 단계는 누군가 승인해야 합니다. osFoundry의 Departments는 이런 일에 "부서"라는 자리를 만들어 주고, 에이전트가 지금 뭘 하는지는 Agent Registry에서 볼 수 있습니다. 부서가 사람, 에이전트, 직무를 가진다 osFoundry 는 채팅, AI 에이전트, 파일, 각종 도구를 한 창에 모은 데스크톱 앱입니다. Departments에서는 부서마다 구성원(사람과 에이전트), 직무(Duties), Department Projects, 기록을 가집니다. 목록에는 부서별 상태와 스폰서가 나오는데, 예시에서는 Customer Support가 일시 중지, Launch Operations가 운영 중이고 그 아래 Press Desk라는 하위 부서가 있으며, Research는 아직 초안입니다. 새로 만든 부서는 초안으로 시작합니다. 자리는 비어 있고 직무는 일시 중지 상태라서, 자리를 채우고 직무를 켜기 전에는 아무것도 돌아가지 않습니다. Desk: 지금 사람이 봐야 할 것 부서를 열면 먼저 Desk가 나옵니다. 처리가 필요한 것을 한 페이지에 모은 화면입니다. Launch Operations 예시에는 이런 것들이 있습니다.

articles.title: Seven Tests I Write Before I Trust a .NET Play Counter
articles.excerpt: A play counter is the easiest feature to demo and one of the easiest to get quietly wrong. plays = plays + 1 passes every manual test you'll ever click through. It also counts a retried request four t…
articles.body: A play counter is the easiest feature to demo and one of the easiest to get quietly wrong. plays = plays + 1 passes every manual test you'll ever click through. It also counts a retried request four times, loses plays when a worker crashes at the wrong moment, and happily lets one script "listen" to a track 2,000 times an hour. So when I built a Spotify-style play count in .NET 10 recently, I didn't start with the counter. I started with the tests that would tell me the counter was lying. Here are seven of them, roughly in the order they bit me. The test bodies are trimmed to the part that matters; where something is cut, the comment says so. articles.body: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA is pushing ahead with its plan to build a moon base for astronauts by 2032, with the agency unveiling up to $10 billion in contracts to launch and deliver cargo to the moon and other efforts on Saturday (Nov. 7). The NASA announcement, revealed here during the space agency's "Max Power" air show event at Kennedy Space Center , included plans for a new $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) framework, dubbed CLPS 2, about$1.3 billion in funding for the agency's Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) program, and the nuclear-powered "PROMISE" rover on the moon.

articles.body: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman knows how to make an entrance. Under the bright afternoon sun on Saturday (Nov. 7), Isaacman plummeted through the air above 10,000 onlookers, skydiving into the agency's air show MAX POWER. MAX POWER overtook NASA's Kennedy Space Center here over the weekend, combining aeronautics and aerospace in a massive public air show, the first of its kind for the space agency. A mix of astronauts, fighter jet displays and new technology on display, the spectacle is a lot space-ier than a traditional air show, and Isaacman made sure to really showcase this merging of worlds.

articles.body: A satellite went knee-deep in the dead, after a voice command from the ground activated the Doom video game in space. Playing a first-person shooter from 1993 was obviously not in the design plan for the PRETTY cubesat , which is run by a consortium including the European Space Agency (ESA). But the pioneering voice command opens up new worlds for satellite work, the team says. "Someone in distress at sea or in a remote area could transmit 'mayday' or "help" on a radio," stated Estonia's Tanagra Space, which supplied the software for the feat. The hope is one day, a satellite could use transcription and AI to alert rescue services for assisting folks in remote zones. The call to play Doom, thankfully, had no other urgency than curiosity — and teamwork, fueled by pizza.

articles.body: 6 Min Read CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars The CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2 crew egress from their simulated Mars habitat, completing their mission on Oct. 31, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. articles.title: The climate case for AI has not been made
articles.excerpt: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on coun…
articles.body: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action. But so far, industries around the world aren’t doing nearly enough to harness the technology to actually drive down the greenhouse-gas emissions heating up the planet, despite some very optimistic claims from AI companies.
